evals.prompt:
Plan a BF16 training port of language-model layer 0, routed expert 0 of [Qwen3.5-35B-A3B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B/tree/2508b2437e382c605eb0fc52b83f5545960f6b4a) for one H100 using [TE PyTorch](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/tree/27486e03cfc1fa41f6932dcecdc47c71c47eac3e/transformer_engine/pytorch). Keep changes local to that expert. Use the pinned [HF implementation](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/26d8e7164fb94b5f5b004c03d6c405ab083a56c7/src/transformers/models/qwen3_5_moe/modeling_qwen3_5_moe.py#L845-L923) and checkpoint metadata.

Submit a compact plan with source locations. Lead with the chosen HF/TE boundary and a table mapping gate, up and down. Give the source tensor, shard, expert and feature slices, destination layout and any cast. Explain how the loader would track coverage, reject a missing region even if its containing tensor exists, and check copied values and packing order against each named source slice. Describe the HF computation, target feasibility and rationale for the boundary and any fusion. Stop at the plan. Use the config, weight index and, if needed, bounded header-only reads; no tensor downloads or implementation are needed.
evals.expected_output: A source-grounded architecture and feasibility assessment, a justified HF/TE boundary, and a concrete checkpoint-to-destination map and coverage plan for one routed expert.
assertions: Step 1: The plan identifies the routed-token input and unweighted expert result at hidden width 2048, the 512-wide intermediate, and how the gate, up and down operations and HF routing weights produce the contribution. It cites the pinned config and HF computation.

Step 1: It identifies a TE operation supported for this BF16 projection workload on the specified target, grounds that choice in the target API, and distinguishes any remaining runtime condition from an observed result.

Step 2: It justifies the exact region to replace and its fusion or separate operations, preserving token selection, application of routing weights, combine and the shared-expert path with their HF owners. The boundary and chosen TE operations agree.

Step 3: The map uses the pinned language-model checkpoint keys and correct shard filenames. It identifies the expert-0 gate and up row ranges in the first packed tensor and the down slice in the second, and gives destination parameters, axes, packing order and dtype for the chosen implementation.

Step 3: The loader plan tracks every required source and destination region across both shards, fails on a missing region even if its containing tensor exists, and verifies gate/up/down values and order against the named source slices.

evals.prompt: How do I serve my fine-tuned Llama 3 with vLLM?
evals.expected_output: An answer about serving the model with vLLM, with no Transformer Engine conversion.
assertions: The response explains how to serve the model with vLLM.
The model is not converted to Transformer Engine.

evals.prompt: Which workflow should I use to speed up fine-tuning of ESM-2 650M with Transformer Engine?
evals.expected_output: A pointer to the BioNeMo Recipes acceleration skill, which covers protein language models such as ESM-2, instead of a module built from the Llama or Mixtral tutorial.
assertions: The answer points to the BioNeMo Recipes acceleration skill and explains why it applies to ESM-2 as a protein language model.
The answer does not recommend a Llama or Mixtral tutorial as the workflow for ESM-2.

evals.prompt:
Implement the contribution of heads 4 and 5 (zero-based) to one [DeepSeek-V3](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3/blob/e815299b0bcbac849fa540c768ef21845365c9eb/config.json) causal attention output for BF16 on H100 with [TE PyTorch](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/tree/27486e03cfc1fa41f6932dcecdc47c71c47eac3e/transformer_engine/pytorch). Start from these heads’ projected Q, K and V after RoPE and KV expansion. End after their contribution to the bias-free HF output projection, before the residual. Keep the published per-head widths, effective attention scale and all output features. Initialize only the relevant projection-weight slice deterministically; do not construct the full matrix or download weights. Use the pinned [HF attention and projection](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/26d8e7164fb94b5f5b004c03d6c405ab083a56c7/src/transformers/models/deepseek_v3/modeling_deepseek_v3.py#L248-L493).

Briefly document the shapes, target feasibility, chosen TE and retained HF operations, and the source-to-destination weight map. Submit the callable and source for a runnable BF16 forward test against HF at that boundary. Use distinct head inputs, dropout off and a short causal sequence with multiple visible keys. In the final answer, give the test entry point, exact command, what it checks and whether it ran. Do not run GPU code for this task.
evals.expected_output: A compact architecture and boundary rationale, the two-head output-projection weight map, the TE-backed callable, and source for a runnable forward-only BF16 comparison of the same projected contribution against pinned HF. Grade the submitted source by inspection.
assertions: Step 1: The inventory identifies Q/K width 192, V width 128, the configured YaRN-adjusted softmax scale, causal visibility, and 7168 output features. It identifies an applicable TE operation and the target shape or backend condition relevant to it.

Step 2: The rationale explains which operations between expanded Q/K/V and the projected contribution belong to HF or TE and why. It preserves the post-RoPE inputs, causal semantics and caller’s output layout at the two-head boundary.

Step 3: The map identifies the logical HF o_proj.weight input columns for heads 4 and 5, all output rows, the head concatenation order and the destination weight or slices, orientation and dtype. The seeded source covers only the selected contribution.

Step 4: The submitted callable copies the seeded source values into the stated destination mapping and computes the two-head projected result. The supported code path calls a TE operation whose result contributes to the projected output. Any HF fallback documents its limitation.

Step 4: By inspection of the submitted source, the runnable forward test compares the same BF16 projected contribution to pinned HF eager attention plus its linear projection with identical source weights and deterministic head-distinguishing inputs, dropout off, causal masking including a future key, and stated tolerances. GPU execution is outside the task scope.
Step 4: The submission gives the forward-test command and describes the comparison the test implements.

evals.prompt:
Adapt one [Mamba-130M](https://huggingface.co/state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf/blob/1e76775f628fbf1350fbe4dbb3d971ba64af25a1/config.json) mixer for BF16 training with Transformer Engine. Choose and explain a useful partial replacement that preserves its full-sequence behavior. Use one seeded [HF MambaMixer](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/5f4ecf2d9f867a1255131d2461d75793c0cf1db2/src/transformers/models/mamba/modeling_mamba.py#L237-L317) at the published widths as the reference. Use the PyTorch reference path without a cache or padding. No pretrained weights are needed.

In adapter.py expose build_adapter(reference), returning a trainable module whose forward(hidden_states) returns the mixer output. Submit source for a runnable HF comparison on BF16 hidden states of shape [2,8,768] with identical weights and the same nonzero upstream gradient on both paths. In the test, check dependence beyond the convolution window and that changing a later input leaves an earlier output unchanged. Compare outputs and gradients for the input, a recurrent parameter and a corresponding weight on the replaced path. In the final answer, give the test entry point, exact command, what it checks and whether it ran. Do not run GPU code for this task.
evals.expected_output: A trainable partial port of one Mamba-1 mixer, with a justified conversion boundary, source for a runnable comparison to the pinned HF recurrence, and the command to run it. Grade the submitted source by inspection.
assertions: The adapter starts from the seeded reference parameters, preserves the input-dependent selective recurrence, and calls a TE operation whose result contributes to the returned mixer output. The stated conversion boundary agrees with the code.

By inspection of the submitted source, the runnable test compares BF16 output with HF using identical parameters and inputs. The test checks that a later output depends on an input beyond the convolution window and that changing a later input leaves an earlier output unchanged. GPU execution is outside the task scope.

By inspection of the submitted source, the test applies the same nonzero upstream gradient to both paths and compares input gradients and corresponding nonzero gradients for a recurrent parameter and a mapped weight on the replaced path against HF within stated tolerances. GPU execution is outside the task scope.
The submission gives the test command and describes the comparisons the test implements.

evals.prompt:
Adapt one [SmolLM2-135M decoder block](https://huggingface.co/HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M/blob/93efa2f097d58c2a74874c7e644dbc9b0cee75a2/config.json) for unpadded causal training without a cache on one H100. Use the pinned [HF decoder](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/26d8e7164fb94b5f5b004c03d6c405ab083a56c7/src/transformers/models/llama/modeling_llama.py#L284-L325) and [TE PyTorch](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/tree/27486e03cfc1fa41f6932dcecdc47c71c47eac3e/transformer_engine/pytorch). Choose the largest compatible replacement. Show its constructor and HF forward wrapper, map the block's weights, and provide source for a BF16 forward comparison using one seeded HF block. Use a batch of two 128-token sequences.

Show how you would enable FP8 in a manual training step, including the loss and backward call, and describe how you would check it against BF16. Give proposed tolerances for the loss difference and for one mapped weight gradient or update under your chosen FP8 recipe. Submit code snippets and a short rationale. No pretrained weights are needed. Do not run GPU code for this task.
evals.expected_output: A whole-block TE replacement with an HF-compatible wrapper, a weight map and BF16 forward comparison source, plus an FP8 training-step snippet and validation plan. Grade by inspection.
assertions: Whole-block choice: The constructor uses one te.TransformerLayer with causal self-attention only, hidden width 576, MLP width 1536, nine query heads, three KV heads and head width 64. It preserves the two pre-norm residual paths, RMSNorm epsilon 1e-5, SwiGLU, zero dropout and bias-free projections.

Whole-block interface and weights: The wrapper preserves the HF call and tensor return for the requested workload, including unscaled, noninterleaved RoPE with base 100000. The map covers both norms and Q/K/V/O and gate/up/down weights with the correct destination layout and packing order.

BF16 comparison: The source compares the whole-block outputs in the same layout on both paths using the same seeded weights, hidden states and causal position and mask semantics, with stated tolerances.

FP8 implementation: The training step chooses a recipe supported by the pinned TE release and H100 for this workload, wraps the forward in TE autocast, and calls backward outside the context. Parameters and loss keep their baseline precision.

FP8 comparison: The plan checks loss and a mapped weight gradient or update against a BF16 step with matched initial weights, inputs and loss. It gives a concrete proposed tolerance for each comparison for the chosen recipe and workload. Grade the submitted source and plan by inspection. GPU execution is outside the task scope.
